styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Zócalo, the great museums and the floating gardens of Xochimilco.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Tacos, markets and street stalls from Roma to Coyoacán.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Aztec ruins, colonial churches and the pyramids at Teotihuacán.

stays.why: Walk to the Zócalo, Templo Mayor and Bellas Artes. Busy by day, quieter at night; use sitio taxis after dark.
Leafy streets, cafés and bars; good for food and nightlife. Easy walking, short ride apps to the center.
Upscale hotels near Chapultepec Park and the anthropology museum. Calm and walkable, pricier restaurants.
Colonial lanes, the Frida Kahlo house and markets. Slower pace; longer rides to the center.

food: Eat tacos al pastor from busy stalls; a few tacos cost M$60–120. Pick places with a crowd and turnover.
Markets are cheap and good: Mercado de San Juan and La Merced for produce, cheese and cooked food.
Try pozole, tamales, chilaquiles and tlayudas. Breakfast at a fonda is often M$80–150.
Drink only bottled or filtered water, and skip ice from street carts if your stomach is sensitive.
Book ahead for top restaurants in Roma and Polanco; walk-ins are hard on weekend nights.
more_time: Swap a city day for Teotihuacán: go early by bus or tour to climb the pyramids before the heat and crowds.
Add a day in Coyoacán for the Frida Kahlo museum (book tickets online) and the markets.
Take a boat (trajinera) at Xochimilco on a weekend; agree the price per boat before boarding.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Centro, one big museum and a Teotihuacán or Coyoacán day without rushing.

month_notes: Jan: cool, dry and clear. Cold mornings around 7°C; pack a jacket.
Feb: mild and dry, one of the best months to walk the city.
Mar: warm and mostly dry; strong sun at midday.
Apr: hot afternoons and little rain; go to ruins early.
May: hotter and wetter; afternoon showers start.
Jun: rainy season begins; carry a rain jacket.
Jul: wettest month; plan indoor museums for afternoons.
Aug: still very wet; mornings are usually clearer.
Sep: heavy rain continues; streets can flood briefly.
Oct: rain eases; comfortable days return.
Nov: dry and mild; good for outdoor sights.
Dec: cool and dry; festive in the Centro, chilly nights.

climate_guide.summary: High-altitude city with mild days all year and a wet summer. Rain falls mostly in afternoon storms from June to September.

items.title: Best time: November to April
items.text: Dry, sunny days around 22–27°C. Ideal for walking, ruins and markets.

items.title: Wet season June to September
items.text: Up to 26–27 rain days a month. Storms usually hit in the afternoon; keep mornings for outdoor plans.

items.title: Cool nights all year
items.text: Lows of 7–13°C. Evenings need a light jacket, especially in December and January.

items.title: Mild, not hot
items.text: Highs stay around 22–27°C. The altitude can make sun feel stronger; use sunscreen.

items.title: Afternoon downpours
items.text: Summer storms are short but heavy. Carry a compact rain jacket and waterproof shoes.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a light rain jacket in summer, comfortable walking shoes and a hat.

transit.best: Metro for cheap fast trips; ride apps for night and cross-town journeys.

modes.text: 12 lines, M$5–6 per ride, 05:00–00:00 weekdays. Very crowded at rush hour; watch your pockets.
Metrobús BRT and trolleybuses cover main avenues; pay with a rechargeable card.
White and magenta taxis: agree the fare or use the meter, and prefer sitio stands at night. Uber, DiDi and inDrive are widely used and cheap; check the plate before getting in.
Driving is slow and parking is hard. Not worth it inside the city.
Best in Centro, Roma and Condesa. Sidewalks are uneven; watch your step.
EcoBici stations in central areas. Helmets are not common.
